lines.japanese: それが一年ちょっと前のことだ。
lines.english: That was a little over a year ago.

lines.japanese: そのあと鳳は、俺をピンフ通りの裏の裏にある古びた商業ビルへ連れていった。
lines.english: Afterward, Otori took me to an aging commercial building deep in the backstreets off Pinfu Street.

lines.japanese: 一階はやる気の感じられない殺風景な中華料理屋。
lines.english: The ground floor held a drab Chinese restaurant that didn't seem to be trying very hard.

lines.japanese: 最上階は聞いたこともない名前の、金利がやばそうなローン会社。
lines.english: The top floor belonged to a loan company I'd never heard of, one whose interest rates looked downright criminal.

lines.japanese: その間を埋めるパブやスナックの看板は、どこか昭和的な郷愁をさそう青や紫の色に灯っていた。
lines.english: Between them, signs for pubs and hostess bars glowed blue and violet with a distinctly Showa-era nostalgia.

lines.japanese: あいつは、おんぼろエレベーターから降りてきたヤクザスーツのおっさんと慣れた感じの会釈を交わして（交わすなよ）、地階へつづく細い急階段を下りていった。
lines.english: Otori exchanged a practiced nod with a middle-aged man in a mobster's suit emerging from the decrepit elevator—don't do that—then descended a narrow, steep staircase into the basement.

lines.japanese: 薄暗い闇の底から吹きあげられてくるのは、内臓に響く四つ打ちのバスとアナログシンセの金属的な旋律。
lines.english: From the dim pit below surged a four-on-the-floor bass pulse that thudded through the guts, threaded with the metallic melody of an analog synth.

lines.japanese: そこはコンビニで売ってる情報誌には決して紹介されないような胡散臭いクラブ。店の名前は、たしかヘテロ……えーと、忘れた。ヘテロなんたら言った気がする。
lines.english: It was the sort of shady club that would never appear in one of those listings magazines sold at convenience stores. Hetero... something, I think it was called. I forget. Pretty sure it started with Hetero.

lines.japanese: 国内の若いアマチュアたちが下積み感覚でレジデンスＤＪを務めるような、良くも悪くも商売っ気のない、サークル的なノリの箱だった。
lines.english: Young Japanese amateurs served as resident DJs there to pay their dues. For better or worse, the place had little interest in profit and the atmosphere of a hobbyist collective.

lines.japanese: エントランスはいまどきＩＤチェックもなく、年齢制限なし・所持品検査なしの万客歓迎オールウェルカム。聞けば登記上はレストランらしく（すぐバレる嘘）、終夜営業も未成年の入店も条例違反ではないらしい。
lines.english: The entrance had no ID check, even in this day and age. No age restriction, no search of your belongings—come one, come all. On paper, it was apparently a restaurant, an obvious lie, which supposedly meant neither all-night operation nor admitting minors violated local ordinances.

lines.japanese: その日ＤＪが回していたのは主にトランス。トランスと言っても、日本の大手企業が躍起になって流行らせた、パチンコ屋＆パラパラギャル御用達の馬鹿明るいアゲアゲ・ハッピーチューンじゃない。
lines.english: That night the DJ played mainly trance. Not the idiotically bright, hands-in-the-air happy tunes for pachinko parlors and Para Para girls that major Japanese companies had strained to turn into a craze.

lines.japanese: ゴリゴリでバキバキでぐにょんぐにょんに曲がる、ゴアとかサイケとかって区分されてる系統のトランス。それはクールに汗をかくための環境音。闇の中で黙々と踊りくるうのに適した、速くて冷たい音のシャワーだ。
lines.english: This was the grinding, pounding, writhing kind of trance classed as Goa or psytrance. Background music for sweating without losing your cool: a fast, cold shower of sound made for dancing yourself mad in silent concentration and darkness.

lines.japanese: そんな激しい音で満たされたコンクリート打ちっぱなしの地下室に、男たちの体臭と女たちの香水、さらにはニコチンとアルコールとカンナビスの香りまで無秩序に溶けあい、その濃密な闇を青や緑のレーザーが貫く。
lines.english: In that bare-concrete basement filled with violent sound, men's body odor and women's perfume dissolved chaotically into nicotine, alcohol, and cannabis. Blue and green lasers pierced the concentrated dark.

lines.japanese: 鳳の言ったとおり、それはまさしく混沌としたアングラ臭ってやつだった。
lines.english: Exactly as Otori had promised: the stink of a chaotic underground.

lines.japanese: 石像のように固まって意識の奥深くを旅する男。誰かれ構わず抱きついてケミカルな幸せを叫ぶ女。柱の陰で粘膜と性感帯を擦りあわせる即席カップル。黒人と白人の殴り合いを止めない真っ赤な髪の日本人スタッフ。
lines.english: A man stood rigid as stone, journeying through the furthest reaches of consciousness. A woman embraced strangers indiscriminately and proclaimed her chemical happiness. A couple who had just met rubbed mucous membranes and erogenous zones behind a pillar. A red-haired Japanese staffer made no attempt to stop a Black man and a white man from beating each other.

lines.japanese: 俺はそんな終わってる光景の数々を、バルコニー状に張りだした二階のラウンジから見下ろしていた。始発電車の動きだす時刻が待ちどおしくて、とてもじゃないけど踊る気分にはなれなかった。
lines.english: I looked down on those scenes of total ruin from a second-floor lounge projecting over the room like a balcony. I could hardly wait for the first train to start running. Dancing was out of the question.

lines.japanese: べつに俺だって、カッチョいい音に合わせて、大勢の知らない誰かと無言で肩をぶつけ合うのが嫌いなわけじゃない。ただああいう、警察に踏みこまれたら面倒なことになりそうな無法地帯は肌に合わないって話だ。
lines.english: It wasn't that I disliked knocking shoulders in silence with a crowd of strangers to a killer track. A lawless hole where a police raid promised complications simply didn't agree with me.

lines.japanese: しかしその観覧席も、完全に隔絶された無菌室というわけではなかった。
lines.english: Unfortunately, even the observation deck was no perfectly isolated clean room.

lines.japanese: 「イェア！　成田君みっけー！」
lines.english: “Yeah! Found you, Narita!”

lines.japanese: 鳳の“見極め”とやらで認められてしまったらしい俺は、やつの仲間たちから大いに歓迎され、あたかも転校初日の小学生みたいに取りかこんで持てなされてしまった。
lines.english: Apparently, Otori's ‘assessment’ had earned me his approval. His companions welcomed me extravagantly, surrounding and fussing over me like a transfer student on his first day of elementary school.

lines.japanese: 「♪そんなところで何してるんだい、オンナとここでナニしたいんだい」
lines.english: “♪ What’re you doing way over there? Wanna do IT with a woman right here?”

lines.japanese: 「ヘイＹＯファッキン成田カモーン、ひとりでシコシコやってねえで早くこっち来いよ。あんたに犯されたくて俺たちゃ朝からパンツ下ろして待ってんだ、早く熱いのブチこんでくんねえとケツの穴が風邪ひいちまうぜ」
lines.english: “Hey, yo, fuckin’ Narita, come on! Quit jerking around by yourself and get over here. We’ve had our pants down since morning, waiting for you to violate us. If you don’t stick something hot in soon, our assholes are gonna catch cold.”

lines.japanese: あのダジャレ豚が、吹き替え洋画で会得したような例のインチキ口調で語りかけてきた。トランス箱にはまるで馴染まないダボダボのＢボーイファッションが、都会に転校してきた田舎ヤンキーみたいで泣ける。
lines.english: The punning pig addressed me in that phony movie-dub street talk of his. His baggy B-boy clothes belonged so poorly in a trance club that he looked like a country delinquent transferred to the city. It brought tears to my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「聞いたよ、あんた皇帝と引きわけたらしいな。Ｈｕｈ、勃起不全のパグみてえなツラして、とんだドーベルマンだァ。野郎がシラフじゃなかった分を差しひいても、イルなドッグだぜ、しゃぶりつきたくなっちまう」
lines.english: “I heard you fought the Emperor to a draw. Huh. Face like a pug with erectile dysfunction, but you turned out to be one hell of a Doberman. Even allowing for the boss not being sober, you're one ill dog. Makes me wanna suck on you.”

lines.japanese: とりあえずド直球のお下劣ジョークさえ連発しておけば、バッドボーイ・フロムＵＳＡな雰囲気が出ると勘違いしているようだ。
lines.english: He appeared to believe that an endless barrage of blunt obscenity would create an authentic *bad boy from the USA* atmosphere.

lines.japanese: だいたい引きわけたも何も、俺は最初から見ず知らずの馬鹿と野蛮な力比べなんてした覚えはない。仮にそれなりの規則のもとで行うスポーツライクな勝負であれば受けてやってもいいが、おそらくは俺の方が──
lines.english: And what did he mean, a draw? I had never agreed to measure brute strength with some idiot I'd never met. If he proposed an athletic contest conducted under some reasonable body of rules, I might accept, and I would most likely—

lines.japanese: ──と思ったけど、どうでもいいことだし、音楽に負けない声を張るのが面倒だったから主張はしなかった。そのままやつの太い腕に押され、ラウンジにいくつか並ぶテーブル席のひとつへ移る。
lines.english: —but it did not matter, and shouting over the music was too much work, so I let it go. His thick arm herded me toward one of the tables scattered around the lounge.

lines.japanese: 「成田君よう、さっきは尾けまわしたり追っかけたり、色々ワックな真似しちまって悪かったな。ちっとばかし驚いてもらいたかっただけなんだァ、許してくれ。ま、昨日の敵は今日の友・苦情や是非はあろうとも──」
lines.english: “Narita, sorry about all the wack shit before—following you, chasing you around. Just wanted to give you a little surprise. Forgive me. Yesterday's enemy is today's friend; you can gripe, but friendship never ends—”

lines.japanese: 「──っつーことで俺、この街ギバラで『アンコモン』の４代目やってる左右田仙一。クルーのあいだじゃＬＲ２００１で通ってッけど、コールミーどっちでもいんじゃない夜はインザナイ街は繁華街おれはクールガイ」
lines.english: “—so anyway, I'm Senichi Souda, fourth-generation leader of Uncommon here in the streets of Gibara. Crew calls me LR2001, but call me either, call me neither; night in the city, city all gritty, and me looking pretty.”

lines.japanese: 太ったハゲは、四本の指を下に向ける形で右手を差しだしてきた。それも映画で覚えたギャング式シェイクハンドなんだろうか。
lines.english: The fat bald man offered his right hand with four fingers pointed downward. Was this another gangster handshake he’d learned from movies?

lines.japanese: 「はっ」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: 邪魔なので払おうと手を浮かしたら、先に熱い馬鹿力でがっちりと掴まれた。そして体ごと引きよせられブラザー系の熱いハグ。バシバシと背中にスタンプ。
lines.english: I lifted a hand to brush him off, but he grabbed it first with a stupidly powerful grip, yanked me bodily toward him, and pulled me into a hot-blooded bro hug. Then he stamped my back with slap after slap.

lines.japanese: 呆れている俺をよそに、ひとりでセンキゥマイメン、ヨゥ、イヨゥなどと陽気に唱えつづける。袖口から覗く蛇だか竜だかの青黒いスミがかなりに威圧的だけど、あんがい根はいいやつなのかもしれない。
lines.english: Ignoring my disgust, he merrily chanted, ‘Thank you, my man. Yo. Ayo.’ The blue-black ink of a snake or dragon emerging from his sleeve looked deeply intimidating, but perhaps he was surprisingly decent underneath it all.

lines.japanese: 「でー、こいつ、このヒゲだらけのムサ苦しいのが、この街ギバラで『リディム』を仕切ってる島袋。通り名はチケドン。ＤＪチケドン」
lines.english: “And this hairy, sweaty bastard is Shimabukuro, boss of Riddim here in Gibara. Street name Chikedon. DJ Chikedon.”

lines.japanese: 「ヤーマン！　よろぴくネ成田ちゃ～ん、出会った記念にブリッと一服飛んじゃう～？」
lines.english: “Ya man! Nice ta meetchoo, Naritaaa! To celebrate, wanna blaze one and take a fat flight?”

lines.japanese: 俺の左にいた沖縄顔のドレッドヘアが、手巻きくさい怪しげな煙草をかざしてニンマリ笑った。その煙草からは、あまり日本じゃ香らないはずの香りが漂っていた（うん、きっと新種のハーブ煙草なんだろう）。
lines.english: The Okinawan-looking man with dreadlocks to my left grinned and held up a suspicious hand-rolled cigarette. It gave off an aroma one did not ordinarily encounter in Japan. Yes, surely some new variety of herbal cigarette.

lines.japanese: 「でー、こっちのチャラチャラした糞ガキが、この街ギバラの鶴岡工業で二年坊のくせして番張ってるダイスケ。通り名はバニィ。機械科のバニィＤ」
lines.english: “And this flashy little shit is Daisuke, a second-year punk who runs Tsurugaoka Technical here in Gibara. Street name Bunny. Bunny D from the mechanical department.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょりーっす！　よろます、こんびんび～ん！　え・え・え、あのあのチョイ質いっスか、つーか、ぶっちゃけ隼人先輩どこ中のひとスか！」
lines.english: “Yo-ssup! Nice ta meetcha! Good eveninny-evening! Uh-uh-uh, hey, hey, quick question, if that's cool? Like, for real, Hayato, what middle school'd you go to?”

lines.japanese: 俺の右にいたガン黒ロン毛のギャル男が、黄金色にあわ立つプラカップを置いて身を乗りだした。そのカップからは、あまり未成年と縁がないはずの香りが漂っていた（うん、きっと新種の林檎ソーダなんだろう）。
lines.english: The deeply tanned, long-haired party boy to my right set down a plastic cup foaming gold and leaned toward me. It gave off an aroma rarely associated with minors. Yes, surely some new variety of apple soda.

lines.japanese: はあ……なんだこいつら……お近づきになりたくねえ……。
lines.english: Haaah... What the hell was with these guys? I wanted nothing to do with them...

lines.japanese: 「そんで向こう、あそこであの、中国の卓球選手ライクな顔した女といまラブ＆ジョイしてんのがァ……」
lines.english: “And over there, currently getting his love and joy on with that woman who looks like a Chinese table-tennis player…”

lines.japanese: 「長げーよ。も、いーよ何人いんだよ」
lines.english: “This is taking too long. Enough. How many of you are there?”

lines.japanese: 「んぁ、どうだ？　今日は各チームの幹部だけだもんなぁ、２０人ぐらいか？　あー、でも坂本っちゃんら、いま高速スッ飛ばしてこっち向かってんだよなー？」
lines.english: “Hmm, how many? Only team officers tonight, so maybe twenty? Oh, but Sakamoto’s guys are tearing down the highway to get here now, right?”

lines.japanese: 「スノボ組～？　俺んとこには、さっき野島チームからメールあったよ～。今日の合コンの相手、レベル高過ぎて心に深い傷負ったから、俺らと合流して飲みなおしたいとかって」
lines.english: “The snowboard crew? Nojima's team texted me a minute ago. Said the girls at tonight's mixer were so far out of their league they came away emotionally scarred, so they wanna meet up with us and start drinking all over again.”

lines.japanese: 「ウハ、ちょっせー、野島さんマジうけるわー。てゆか、うっそ待って待って。じゃ何、みんな戻ってくんの？　だはっ、そら鬼だろ、メンバー急増にも程があンだろ。倍率ドンさらに倍、みたいなぎゃははは」
lines.english: “Whoa, pathetic! Nojima's hilarious. Wait, seriously—everybody's coming back? Hah, that's brutal. Talk about a population explosion. Double the stakes—then double them again! Gyahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃははつっておまえ、そんな、２０の倍の倍つったら６０かよ」
lines.english: “Gyahaha? If you double twenty twice, that’s sixty.”

lines.japanese: 「んにゃ、２０の倍の倍でしょ。８０じゃん」
lines.english: “Nah, double twenty and double it again. That’s eighty.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～え？　ちょーっとチケドンさ～ん、そら流石にヤバくないスかあ？　まァまァ、俺もひとのこと言えるほど利口じゃねースけどお、にしたって、いくら何でも２０×３ぐらいはさぁ、ぷぷぷ」
lines.english: “Whaaat? Hold on, Chikedon, isn't that a little dangerous? I mean, I'm not exactly a genius myself, but even I know it's twenty times three... Pfft.”

lines.japanese: 「やめろバニィ、口を閉じるんだ。そしてクソみてえな正答と、目上の者への敬意とを秤にかけな」
lines.english: “Stop, Bunny. Close your mouth. Weigh your shitty correct answer against respect for your elders.”

lines.japanese: 「エー、でも俺べつに間違ったことゆってないすぃー。てかチケドンさん、葉っぱキマり過ぎちゃってアタマ回ってねンじゃねー？　ぎゃはは……って痛たたた！」
lines.english: “Whaaat? I didn't say anything wrong, sooo? Maybe Chikedon's smoked so much leaf his brain won't turn over. Gyahaha—ow, ow, ow!”

lines.japanese: 「いいかこのファッキン・ジニアス！　ちっとばかし算数が出来るからって調子こいてんじゃねえ！　ここがロスだったらオメエは今ごろ、ケツの穴に真珠入りのぶってえ礼儀作法をブチ込まれてるとこだぜ！」
lines.english: “Listen, you fucking genius! Don't get cocky just because you can do a little arithmetic! If this were L.A., somebody would be shoving a thick, pearl-studded lesson in manners straight up your ass!”

lines.japanese: 「あた、あたたた……サーセン、サーセンした！」
lines.english: “Ow, ow-ow-ow... M'bad! M'bad, sir!”

lines.japanese: 「チケドン、おまえもつまんねえ間違いを気にするこたぁねえ。いや、何も言うな。いい、いい、言わなくていい。どうせちょっとぐれー算数が出来たって、そんなもん社会に出りゃ処女膜ひとつ守っちゃくれねえんだ」
lines.english: “Chikedon, don't worry about one worthless little mistake. No, don't say anything. It's fine. No need. Once you're out in society, a little arithmetic won't protect so much as a single hymen.”

lines.japanese: 「あーもう、ええわいええわい！　好きに言うがええわい、こうなりゃ俺すっぱー！　すっぱー！」
lines.english: “Ah, whatever, whatever! Say what you want. I’m smoking now! Smoke, smoke!”

lines.japanese: 「おわ出たッ！　チケドンさん必殺、ツイン爆吸い！　ま、タバコですケドネー！」
lines.english: “Whoa, there it is! Chikedon’s finishing move: the Twin Mega-Drag! They’re cigarettes, though!”

lines.japanese: 「Ｕｍ、もったいねえなあ。それ南米直送の良ネタだろ、ちゃんと肺に溜めろ肺にィ。ま、タバコだけどな」
lines.english: “Um, what a waste. That’s quality product straight from South America. Hold it properly in your lungs. Though it’s a cigarette.”

lines.japanese: 「もわぁ～ん、つってブリブリ～ん……つって、あれぇなんで成田っち三人いんの～、つってぶひゃひゃひゃ！　ま、タバコなんだけどね～つって、あはははははははは、アレえ何の話だっけ～？」
lines.english: “Fwoooosh, I’m getting blazed… Wait, why are there three Naritas? Buhyahaha! It’s just a cigarette, though. Ahahahahahaha! Wait, what were we talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「何っつうか、べつに俺らの話に筋とか意味なんかねースけど、えっと６０人だか８０人だかって話？」
lines.english: “I mean, our conversations don’t really have a point or meaning, but… something about sixty or eighty people?”

lines.japanese: 「ママママジでえ！　だはははは！　ろ、ろく、ろくじゅう～？　ひっ、ひいっ、は、ははは腹イテエ～、ぶははは、ちょちょ超ウケる、ろく、６０万て！　ろろろ６０万人はねーわ、ぎゃははははは～！」
lines.english: “S-s-seriously?! Dahahaha! S-six... sixty? Hee—hahahaha, my stomach! Buhahaha, th-that's fucking hilarious! S-six hundred thousand people! Gyahahahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「ねーわって、そりゃあんたの方がねーわ。６０万て。どんだけドンギマリすか」
lines.english: “What’s impossible is *you*. Six hundred thousand? How high are you?”

lines.japanese: 「セイグーッ！　おうよチケドン、いいこと言ったぜえ～？　ザッツライ、俺たちのスケイルは事実なんかにゃ縛られねえ。ユーシー？」
lines.english: “That's gooood! Damn right, Chikedon, you said it! That's right—our scale ain't bound by facts. You see?”

lines.japanese: 「てえわけで成田君。俺らのファミリー、人呼んで柳木原フレイムバーズの構成員は公称６０万人だ。これが俺なりのリアル。異論はあるかいマイブラザー」
lines.english: “So there you have it, Narita. Our family—the organization known as the Yanagihara Flame Birds—officially numbers six hundred thousand. That's my reality. Got a problem with it, my brother?”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　ああ、いや、いんじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. Nah, sounds fine.”

lines.japanese: いきなり問いかけられたが、ほとんど聞いてなかったので適当な返事をした。
lines.english: The question came without warning, but I had barely listened, so I answered at random.

lines.japanese: やつらのノリに馴染めなかった俺は、いつの間にか階下の熱狂に意識を奪われていた。
lines.english: Unable to get into their rhythm, I had somehow let the frenzy downstairs steal my attention.

lines.japanese: アホな男たちの実のない会話より、ハイアングルから鑑賞するねーちゃんたちのキャミソールの胸元の方がよほど退屈を凌げる。
lines.english: Compared with the empty chatter of idiotic men, the camisole necklines of women viewed from above offered far greater relief from boredom.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい成田君よう、ちゃんと聞いてんのかあ？」
lines.english: “Hey, Narita, are you even listening?”

lines.japanese: 「お？　おお、聞いてる聞いてる。アレだろ、６０万だろ。６０万人オー、柳木原なんちゃらーずイェー」
lines.english: “Hmm? Yeah, sure, listening. Six hundred thousand, right? Six hundred thousand, ohhh, Yanagihara Something-or-Others, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 俺は自分のコーラを掴んで、適当にハゲたちのプラカップやアルミ缶にぶつけた。
lines.english: I picked up my cola and carelessly knocked it against the bald men’s plastic cups and aluminum cans.

lines.japanese: 背伸び盛りのティーンや体ばかり育ってしまったヤングアダルトがわらわら寄ってくる柳木原には、良識あるひとびとが「不良の集まり」と眉をひそめる、品のよろしくないグループが大小いくつかあった。
lines.english: Yanagihara drew crowds of teens desperate to seem older and young adults whose bodies had outgrown the rest of them. Among them were several unsavory groups of various sizes—the sort respectable people lumped together as delinquent gangs.

lines.japanese: それはミラー張りのガラスを見るや大音量を垂れながすダンスチームだったり、倉庫や駐車場で胡乱なパーティーを開くレイヴサークルだったり、夜の環状線を時速１００マイルでブッ飛ばすルーレット族だったり──
lines.english: Some were dance teams that blasted music whenever they found mirrored glass. Others were rave circles holding suspicious parties in warehouses and parking lots, or highway racers flying around the beltway at a hundred miles an hour—

lines.japanese: ──と実態は様々あるらしいが、ともかくその夜、そのクラブには、それぞれの集団を束ねている各リーダーたちが多数集められていた。定例会みたいなものらしい。しょーもないサミットもあったもんだ。
lines.english: —apparently the details varied. Anyway, that night a whole bunch of the leaders of these different groups had gathered at the club. Some kind of regular meeting, I guess. What a worthless little summit.

lines.japanese: 「ででででもさー、あ～の、ちょっと言わせてもらっちゃうとさー。ろろろ６０万ってあの、ビミョーに半端じゃな～い？」
lines.english: “B-b-but, um, if I can just say one thing… Isn’t six hundred thousand kind of an awkward number?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　どこが。フツーに切りのいい……」
lines.english: “Huh? How? It’s perfectly round—”

lines.english: “No! No, he’s absolutely right! That’s Chikedon for you. The man’s eye is in orbit. I’m seriously blown away.”

lines.japanese: 「誰がランドサットじゃあ！　つって、でも結局んとこ人間ってみんな宇宙の一部だしねぇ、つってあの、みみみみんな忘れてるかもしれないけど１００億年ぐらい前は星も命も心も神もごた混ぜの一個だったし……」
lines.english: “Who're you calling Landsat?! I mean, when you get down to it, we're all part of the universe, y'know? I mean, um, e-e-e-everybody might've forgotten, but ten billion years ago, stars and life and hearts and gods were all mixed together as one...”

lines.japanese: 「アレえ？　俺いま何しゃべってたあ？」
lines.english: “Huh? What was I talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「バーカ！　知るかよ、そりゃこっちが聞きてえっつうの、ぎゃははは！」
lines.english: “Idiot! How should I know? That’s what *we’d* like to ask! Gyahaha!”

lines.japanese: ああ、やっぱこのノリは無理だ。付いていけねー。俺はふたたびギャルウォッチングへ戻ることにした。
lines.english: Yeah, no. I couldn’t handle their whole vibe. Couldn’t keep up. I returned to watching girls.

lines.japanese: 「そー、だから６０万でしょー。だからコレこの際さー、もー気持ち盛っとかねー？」
lines.english: “Right, so six hundred thousand. Since we’re here, shouldn’t we pad it out a little?”

lines.japanese: 「ＯＫホーミーズ。そんじゃあ６０万・四捨五入すっか。したらおまえミリオン突破だぜえ」
lines.english: “Okay, homies. Let's round six hundred thousand up. That takes us past a million.”

lines.english: “For reaaal?! Uh-uh-uh, then we're going to trillions?! All the way to trillions?! Isn't a trillion a little too out! Of! Con! Troool?!”

lines.japanese: 「ノンノンノ～ン！　ためらうな、ためらうな若者よ！　ためらわない俺たちは！　何故なら！　何故ならば！　何故かと申さば！　ビコーズ申さば！　ウィーアー……」
lines.english: “No, no, nooo! Don't hesitate! Don't hesitate, young man! We do not hesitate! Because! Becaaause! And why, you may inquire! Be-causeth, I declareth! We are...”

lines.japanese: 「はーい、ここでエビバデ・タロップ！」
lines.english: “All right, everybody—hands up!”

lines.japanese: 「らーらー、隼人先輩も手ぇ上げて！」

lines.japanese: 「ウィーアー！」

lines.japanese: いやいやいや、残念じゃない残念じゃない。

lines.english: “I mean… aren’t you people a little old for this?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶはー直球！　ええ～成田っち、そういうこと言っちゃう系～？」
lines.english: “Bwah, direct hit! Come on, Narita, you're the type who says stuff like that?”

lines.english: “He said it? Seriously? Just comes right out and says it? Damn, Hayato, you're one hell of a sadist!”

lines.japanese: 「レァリー？　許してくれんの？　センキゥ、ヨァクール！　さすがだぜ成田君、寛大なるビチグソ野郎だ。よし、俺がプレジデントになった日にゃあ、秘書のアソコにあんたのケツの穴の名を付けよう。ハッハー」

lines.japanese: 「だら恐い！　あーンも、やっぱそーゆーノリじゃん？　こえーんだよ隼人先輩。ちょ、そのツラで表出てみって、女子とかみんなブシャ漏らしだぜ。やべえよマジで、ここはとりま笑っとけって」

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻いてから、コーラを静かに一口飲んだ。

lines.japanese: 「えー……あんさ、じゃ逆に聞くけどさ、な？　ついさっき自分へ襲いかかろうとしてた通り魔にだよ、な？　そんなん相手にいきなり友好的な表情を作れちゃう人間とかいんの」

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」

lines.japanese: 「思いだしてくれよ、俺にあんたを襲えっつーたのは、あのわがままエンペラーだ。ユーシー？」
lines.english: “Remember, it was that selfish Emperor who told us to attack you. You see?”

lines.japanese: ハゲは指ピストルの銃口側を下に向け、撃鉄の方でテーブルみっつ向こうの席を差した。

lines.japanese: このフロアの椅子はどれもシンプルなスチール製なのに、何故かそこにだけ唯一、場違いすぎるベルベットのソファーがあった。
lines.english: Every chair on this level was made of simple steel. Yet there, inexplicably and alone, stood a velvet sofa so spectacularly out of place.

lines.japanese: その王座に深々と埋もれていたのはあいつ。オオトリカケル。
lines.english: Deep within that throne sprawled the man himself. Kakeru Otori.

lines.japanese: 一筋縄ではいかないサル山のボスたちを、今宵、ひと所に召集したキングオブキングス。ギャング気取りのやんちゃ坊主さえ一目を置く悪の華。強大なる無冠の帝王。
lines.english: The king of kings who had assembled the unruly bosses of this monkey mountain in one place tonight. The flower of evil, respected even by boys who played at gangster. A mighty uncrowned emperor.

lines.japanese: やつはワイン色のソファーの上、獲物待ちの軟体動物みたいな姿勢で重たい音楽を浴びていた。しかし俺たちの視線に気付くとわずかに頭を起こし、ぎらりと目を剥くように笑った。
lines.english: He lay on the wine-colored sofa like a mollusk awaiting prey, bathing in the heavy music. But when he noticed our gaze, he raised his head a fraction and smiled, eyes glittering wide.

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに笑うとこじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “There’s nothing to laugh at.”

lines.japanese: キモいから目を逸らした。
lines.english: It was revolting, so I looked away.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、うちの皇帝キホン笑ってッから」
lines.english: “Yeah, our Emperor’s basically always smiling.”

lines.japanese: 「笑うねー。楽しくても笑うし、怒っても笑うし、ヘコんでも笑うねー。ちうか寝てても笑ってるねー」
lines.english: “He smiles when he’s happy. Smiles when he’s angry. Smiles when he’s depressed. Hell, he smiles in his sleep.”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃはは、寝ててもだよ、すごくね？　つか、なんだよソレ、ありえなくね？　やっべー、皇帝たぶん女とやるときもこうだぜ、こんな、腰振りながら、ハハッ！　ハハッ！　ハハーって」
lines.english: “Gyahaha! Even in his sleep. Isn’t that insane? What the hell? Bet the Emperor does it with women too. Thrusting his hips like, ‘Hah! Hah! Hahaa!’”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……そういや俺に刃物向けてるときでも笑ってたなあ」
lines.english: “Yeah… Come to think of it, he was smiling when he held a knife on me.”

lines.japanese: なにもんだ、あいつは。
lines.english: What the hell was he?

lines.japanese: しかし結論から言うと、鳳は俺のぶつけた質問に対して何ひとつ明確に答えやしなかったのだ。
lines.english: The short version was that Otori never gave me a clear answer to a single question I put to him.

lines.japanese: なぜ俺に興味を持ったのか。なぜ俺を尾けてきたのか。なぜ俺にふっかけてきたのか。ふざけんなてめえ。
lines.english: Why was he interested in me? Why had he followed me? Why had he picked a fight? Fuck you, asshole.

lines.japanese: さあなあ。なぜだろうなあ。そうしたかったからだろうなあ。ふざけちゃいねえよ──やつの答えはどれもこれも釈然としないものだった。
lines.english: Who knows? Why indeed? Probably because I wanted to. I'm not fucking with you—every answer he offered was equally unsatisfying.

lines.japanese: 俺はプラカップを置いてハゲたちに聞いた。
lines.english: I set down my plastic cup and asked the bald men.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。あの鳳ってのは何なの」
lines.english: “So. What’s the deal with that Otori guy?”

lines.japanese: 国王たちの囲むテーブルがどっと湧いた。
lines.english: The table of kings erupted.

lines.japanese: 「ハッハー、最初ビビったろ。つか引くよなァ、だってアレ、完璧キャラ作ってんもんなァ」
lines.english: “Hah-ha! Freaked you out at first, right? Course it did. He's built that whole persona from the ground up.”

lines.japanese: 「『ハハハ！　憐れなカスどもよ、舞いあがれ俺に！』」
lines.english: “‘Hahaha! Take wing and rise to me, you pitiful scum!’”

lines.japanese: 「っぽい！　っぽいんだけど、なんか似てない！」
lines.english: “That’s the vibe! But somehow the impression’s completely wrong!”

lines.japanese: 「ま、やめときな成田君。あの男に関しちゃあ、リアルが見えねえソウルが透けねえ、ラベル比べる意味がねえ」
lines.english: “Take my advice, Narita, and leave it alone. His real stays hidden, his soul won’t show; compare all the labels you like and you still won’t know.”

lines.japanese: 「同感～。俺らももう、あのひとの素性とか目論見とか、細けーこと考えんのやめたもんねー？」
lines.english: “Agreed. We stopped thinking about little details like who he really is or what he’s planning ages ago.”

lines.japanese: 「そーそーそ。ほら俳優でさあ、私生活ナゾに包まれちゃってる系の大御所とかいんじゃん。翔さんって、あんな感じかも。なんか庶民が軽々しく触れちゃいけねー的な？　つうかま、実際スゲんだけど」
lines.english: “Right, right. You know those legendary actors whose private lives are wrapped in mystery? Kakeru's kind of like that. Like ordinary people shouldn't touch him carelessly? Besides, he really *is* incredible.”

lines.japanese: 「何すげえって。どうすげえの」
lines.english: “Incredible how?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、すげえ強えーし？」
lines.english: “Well, he’s insanely strong.”

lines.japanese: 「すげえ顔利くし？」
lines.english: “Knows everybody who matters.”

lines.japanese: 「すげえ気前いいし？」
lines.english: “And he’s crazy generous.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: どうやら腕力にあかして威張りちらしているだけの憎まれっ子というわけでもなく、それなりに王たちから敬意を払われている良君のようだった。
lines.english: Apparently he was no despised tyrant who merely threw his strength around. He seemed a decent ruler who commanded real respect from the kings.

lines.japanese: 「あと、すげえ笑える」
lines.english: “Also, he’s fucking hilarious.”

lines.japanese: 「あと、すげえ頭おかしい」
lines.english: “Also, he’s completely insane.”

lines.japanese: 「あと、すげえ寂しがり屋」
lines.english: “Also, he gets incredibly lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「ふ、ふーん……」
lines.english: “H-huh…”

lines.japanese: しかも適度に親しみを持たれているようだ。

lines.japanese: 「ま、でもグラフィティの腕は素直に認めるぜ。断言する、もしあんたがこの街ギバラの壁で、やべえと思えるクールなスプレー絵に出くわしたら、そりゃあ九割方カケルの描いたモンだ」
lines.english: “Still, I’ll give him this: the man can paint. I guarantee you, if you see a spray piece on a wall in Gibara and think, damn, that’s cool, nine times out of ten it’s Kakeru’s.”

lines.japanese: 「俺ゃーそういうのは分かんねーけど、彼がこういう溜まり場を用意してくれんのがありがたくてさあ。人数多いとなかなかね、金かかんねーで警察呼ばれねーで朝までダベれるとこって、コレ何気にないんだよね」
lines.english: “I don't understand that stuff, but I appreciate him finding us hangouts like this. With a crowd this big, there really aren't many places where you can talk till morning without spending money or getting the cops called.”

lines.japanese: 「あと助かんのがさー。ああ、この辺しきってるデカい組が３つあんだけど。あのひと、そっち方面のヤッちゃんにもパイプ持っててー。なんで、調子こいたガキがトラブったりしても、上手いことケツ持ってくれたり」
lines.english: “And another big help—there are three major syndicates running this area. He's got connections with the mob too. So when some cocky kid starts trouble, he can smooth things over and cover our asses.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: なんつーか、聞けば聞くほど関わりたくない世界だ。
lines.english: The more I heard, the less I wanted anything to do with this world.

lines.japanese: 「Ｙｏ、そんなことよりミスタ成田、むしろ俺ァあんたのリアルが知りてえなあ、マイメン」
lines.english: “Yo, enough about that, Mr. Narita. What I wanna know is the real you, my man.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな、たとえば部屋聴きの音楽はどんな感じよ。おっと、行きずりのビッチが股間で奏でるセレナーデ、なァんて答えはなしだぜ。ほんじゃよ、ヒップホップで言ったら東海岸・西海岸、どっち寄りよ？」
lines.english: “Let's say, what music do you play in your room? Whoa, no answers about the serenade some passing bitch plays on your crotch. In hip-hop terms, you East Coast or West Coast?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやレゲエっしょ。レゲエはオネーチャンたち腰クネクネだし、目ェでも楽しいからね。んー、マグロなハニーに泣かされてる成田っちには、定番だけどスウィートなクラシックダンスホールを勧めとくよ～ん」
lines.english: “Nah, reggae. Reggae makes the girls roll their hips, so your eyes have fun too. Narita, if some dead-fish honey's been making you cry, I recommend the classic sweetness of old-school dancehall.”

lines.japanese: 「エーイ、ヨーウ！　エビバリ、リッスンナップ、ナ～ウ！　踊りつかれてヘタってる場合じゃあねえぞＵｈ、この街ギバラの糞ったれボーイズェ～ン、あば・ずれ・ガァァァールズ！」
lines.english: “Ayy, yo! Everybody listen up, now! This ain’t no time to be worn out from dancing, uh! All you shit-kicking boys—and loose-ass giiirls—of Gibara!”

lines.japanese: 「♪指揮者に注もーく、マイク通じ放つ俺の言葉ひびくフロア！　いきなり沈もーく、退屈～で鼻つまみの大人ソレがぉ前ら！　がしかしチームヮーク、毎度ツーカーつうか愛で通過～、これまさに俺たちの通貨！」
lines.english: “♪ Eyes on the conductor, hear my words ring through the floor! Sudden hush—you boring grown-ups, nobody can stand you anymore! But teamwork—we read each other, love gets us through! That love is our currency, coming straight to you!”

lines.japanese: ダミ声のマシンガンラップに応えて、ハゲの近辺からオオーッ！？と期待を孕んだ蛮声があがった。
lines.english: His gravel-voiced machine-gun rap drew a roar of anticipation from the people around him.

lines.japanese: その声が狼煙となり、たちまち背を向けていた者は振りかえる、腰かけていた者は立ちあがる、男も女も走りよる。歓喜の拍手喝采が隅々まで伝播して、誰かのでたらめな指笛がピーピー響いた。
lines.english: That shout went up like a signal flare. Those facing away turned; those sitting sprang to their feet; men and women came running. Delighted cheers and applause rippled into every corner, while somebody's tuneless finger-whistle shrilled above it all.

lines.japanese: 「は？　はあっ？　なんだこりゃあ？」
lines.english: “Huh? The hell? What is this?”

lines.japanese: 「イェア！　ヨウ、ＤＪチケドン、ミュージッ・クモーン」
lines.english: “Yeah! Yo, DJ Chikedon—drop it!”

lines.japanese: 「ひゃはー！　まっか・せって・ちょー！」
lines.english: “Hyahaa! Leave! It! To me!”

lines.japanese: レゲエ野郎が酒と煙草を捨ててカウンターへ走った。客と見分けがつかない格好の店員たちは、しょーがねえなあという呆れ笑顔であっさりやつを中へ通してしまう。客も客なら店も店だ。
lines.english: The reggae freak ditched his drink and cigarette and dashed behind the bar. The staff, dressed so much like the customers you could hardly tell them apart, let him through with nothing more than a weary grin. The customers were bad enough; the establishment was just as hopeless.

lines.japanese: 「ヤーマン、エビバデ・ジョスク～ル！　みんな、チョット・待ってて・ね～え！」
lines.english: “Ya man, everybody chill! Everybody wait! One little minute, okay?”

lines.japanese: 飛び入りＤＪは使われていなかったラウンジ用のターンテーブルに貼りつくと、べろり舌なめずり、片手でツマミやらダイヤルやらを操作しつつ、残る手にマイクを握った。
lines.english: The impromptu DJ planted himself at the unused lounge turntables and licked his lips. One hand went to work on the knobs and dials while the other seized a microphone.

lines.japanese: 「エ～イ！　先走り大好きなオトコノコも～？　お股かっぴろげのオネーチャンも～？」
lines.english: “Ayy! All you boys who just looove coming early! All you ladies with your legs spread wiiide!”

lines.japanese: 「まずは待とう！　まずは落ちつこう！　逸る気持ちおさえ猛る心しずめ！　まずは前戯からだカラダ立てる力だから宝濡らす刀だから！」
lines.english: “First we wait! First we take it slow! Rein in the urge and soothe that savage soul! Foreplay comes first—strength to raise the body, wet the treasure, draw the sword!”

lines.japanese: 低俗なユーモアが妙な緩急付きで乱射され、そのくだらない才能を聴衆が囃したてているうち、やがてどっしりした重めのリズムトラックがスピーカーから這いずりでてきた。
lines.english: Lowbrow jokes flew in a barrage with a bizarre command of pace, and while the crowd cheered on that perfectly worthless talent, a thick, heavy rhythm track finally crawled from the speakers.

lines.japanese: 「チェキラーゥ！　イッツァ、ショウ、ターイ！」
lines.english: “Check it out! It’s showtime!”

lines.japanese: ハゲがレフェリーよろしく、睨みあうガキふたりのあいだに立つ。
lines.english: Baldy stepped between the glaring kids like a referee.

lines.japanese: 「今宵の熱闘バウト一発目かましやがるご機嫌なファッキンボーイズにＨＥＹヨウプリーズ、クラップ・ヨァ・ハーンズ！　まずはチャンピオン、ご存知ラテン系お兄番長こいつがダイスケ土門、ａｋａバニィＤだ！」
lines.english: “Tonight's first red-hot bout is brought to you by two fine fuckin' boys, so hey, yo—please, clap your hands! First, the champion! You know him, you love him, the Latin big brother of bad boys himself: Daisuke Domon, a.k.a. Bunny D!”

lines.japanese: 「ウェーイ！　あざまァーす！　あざまァーす！」
lines.english: “Wheyy! 'Preci-aaate it! 'Preci-aaate it!”

lines.japanese: 「これに立ちむかいやがんのがァ、ＹＦＢ期待のホープにして、皇帝に見出されし天馬！　下馬評では圧倒的に不利だが、その屈辱で負け犬根性に火を付けやがれ！　炎のチャレンジャー！　カズマ森里インダハウス！」
lines.english: “And stepping up to face him: the bright young hope of the YFB, the Pegasus handpicked by the Emperor! The odds say he ain't got a prayer, but let that humiliation set his underdog soul on fire! The challenger in flames! Kazuma Morisato in the house!”

lines.japanese: きゃー、うおー、ひゅーひゅーひゅーと沸きたつ群衆。一方、玉座に埋もれた酔いどれ皇帝は、気だるげな薄笑いを浮かべて静かに開戦を待っている。
lines.english: The crowd erupted—screams, roars, whistles. Meanwhile the drunken Emperor, sunk deep into his throne, waited for hostilities to commence with a languid little smirk.

lines.japanese: そして野次馬にぐるり囲まれて対峙するロン毛とロン毛は、すでに互いのデコを擦りつけんばかりの超々至近距離で、熾烈なメンチ合戦を始めていた。
lines.english: The two longhairs faced each other inside a solid ring of spectators, already close enough to grind foreheads as they waged a savage war of dirty looks.

lines.japanese: 「あほくせ……要はこいつら、バカ騒ぎするきっかけが欲しかっただけじゃねえか」
lines.english: “Stupid as hell... All they wanted was an excuse to make a racket.”

lines.japanese: どうせ聞こえやしないので、俺は堂々とブーたれながら輪を抜けだした。
lines.english: No one could hear me anyway, so I slipped out of the circle, grumbling without a shred of shame.

lines.japanese: しかし皇帝陛下には近付きたくなかったので、仕方なくカウンターへ身を寄せる。その内側ではレゲエ風が、ユラユラ揺れながら次に回すべきアナログ盤を選んでいた。
lines.english: I didn't want to get any closer to His Imperial Majesty, though, so the bar was my only refuge. Behind it, Reggae swayed gently as he picked the next record to spin.

lines.japanese: 「おっさん、ところでａｋａってなに」
lines.english: “Hey, old man. What’s a.k.a. mean, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「んあー、ａｓ　ｋｎｏｗｎ　ａｓの略。アつまり“またの名をー”みたいな？」
lines.english: “Mmm? Short for *also known as*. You know—‘otherwise called,’ that sorta thing?”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 輪の内側ではついに決戦の火ぶたが切って落とされたようだが、どうでもいい。俺は口の中でブロックアイスをごろごろ転がしながら考えた。ＨＡＹＡＴＯ成田、またの名をダンディーＨ──
lines.english: It looked like battle had finally begun inside the circle. Whatever. I rolled a block of ice around my mouth and gave the matter some thought. Hayato Narita, a.k.a. Dandy H—

lines.japanese: ──ナシだな。なんだか前戯が無駄にねちっこいエロオヤジみたいだ。
lines.english: —No. Sounds like some dirty old man who spends needlessly long on foreplay.

lines.japanese: 「ちょーっ！　も何してんの止めれって！　何なんソレ、当事者が華麗にガン無視とかどんだけだーもう！」
lines.english: “Hey! What are you doing? Stop them! What is *with* you? You're one of the people involved and you're just ignoring it like a pro!”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: カウンターに肘をついてボケッと突っ立っていたら、あの合体ロボみたいな仇名で呼ばれていた小娘が、いつの間にか俺の腕を気安く叩いていた。なんだ、馴れ馴れしいサルしかいないのか、この空間は。
lines.english: While I stood there zoned out with one elbow on the bar, the girl with the combining-robot nickname had apparently come over and started slapping my arm like we were old friends. Was every last person in this place an overfamiliar ape?

lines.japanese: 「ねーねーね知ってんしょー？　バニィ君ガチで空手やってんしー、カズ君なんかカンペキ圏外だよ。ヤバいヤバい、無理だってあんなん、マッハで秒殺だって」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, hey, you know, right? Bunny seriously trains in karate and stuff. Kazu's completely out of his league. This is bad, seriously bad—he can't do this. He'll get wasted in, like, half a second!”

lines.japanese: ぺっ。俺は口の中の氷をグラスに吐きもどしてから言った。
lines.english: Ptuh. I spat the ice in my mouth back into the glass before answering.

lines.japanese: 「なんで。知るわけねーじゃん。俺、部外者だもん」
lines.english: “How would I know? I’m an outsider.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: やつは顔を前へ突きだして目を見開いた。俺が部外者なのを知らないってことは、こいつもこいつで部外者なのかもしれない。
lines.english: She thrust her face forward, eyes wide. If she didn’t know I was an outsider, maybe she was one herself.

lines.japanese: 「え、そーなん？　……ですか？」
lines.english: “Oh, really? I mean... you're not with them, sir?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、カンペキ部外者じゃん」
lines.english: “I mean, I’m obviously an outsider.”

lines.japanese: 俺はだらりと両手を広げた。おら、上から下までとくと見やがれ。フリマと古着屋で揃えたこの平凡きわまる善良な小市民コーディネイトを。
lines.english: I let both arms hang open. Go on, take a good long look, top to bottom. Behold this supremely ordinary, upstanding-citizen ensemble, assembled from flea markets and used-clothes shops.

lines.japanese: ジーンズは多少ほころんじゃいるが、ダメージ加工なんて洒落たもんじゃない、ただ現場で釘ひっかけただけだ。戦車色のフライトジャケットは街中あふれてるＮ－２Ｂタイプ。タイプであって、レプリカですらない。
lines.english: The jeans were frayed in places, sure, but it wasn't any stylish distressing. I'd just snagged them on a nail at work. The tank-green flight jacket was the same N-2B type you saw everywhere in town—and *type* was the word. It wasn't even a replica.

lines.japanese: 「え、でも責任とってよ！　だってこうなったん、部外者がカズ君にコーラ頼んだからじゃん！」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, take responsibility! This only happened because some outsider asked Kazu for a cola!”

lines.japanese: 「コーラじゃねえよ、ウイスキーコーク・ウイスキー抜きだよ」
lines.english: “It wasn’t a cola. It was a whiskey Coke, hold the whiskey.”

lines.japanese: そのとき、どわっと悲鳴やら歓声やらが膨れあがった。ちょいと爪先立って人の輪の中央を覗くと──
lines.english: Just then the screams and cheers swelled. I rose onto my toes for a look at the center of the ring—
“Seiyah!”

lines.japanese: ──ガッツポーズよろしく空手の型を結ぶギャル男の足元で、茶髪の方が腹を押さえて膝をついている。
lines.english: —and there stood the pretty boy, striking a karate pose with his fists clenched in triumph, while the brown-haired kid knelt at his feet clutching his stomach.

lines.japanese: ゴングが鳴ってものの数十秒、早くもチャンピオンのクリーンヒットが決まったようだ。すぐにハゲ審判がゥワン、トゥー、ツリーと嘘くさい発音の数字を重ねてゆく。しかし。
lines.english: Only a few dozen seconds after the bell, the champion had already landed clean. The bald referee immediately began counting, ‘Wahn, twoo, three,’ in a phony accent. But—

lines.japanese: 「か、痒くもねぇ……こんなんんん……！」
lines.english: “D-doesn't even... itch... something like this...!”

lines.japanese: カウント５と待たず、茶髪はよろめきながらも立ちあがった。いいぞいいぞとギャラリーが沸く。
lines.english: Before the count reached five, the brown-haired kid staggered back to his feet. The gallery roared its approval.

lines.japanese: 「なー！　立っちゃった、あほだ！　なに立ってん、あのばかー！」
lines.english: “See! He got up! Idiot! Why’d he get up, that moron!”

lines.japanese: 今度は腕を連打されて、俺の注意は小娘に引きもどされた。
lines.english: Now she was drumming on my arm, dragging my attention back to her.

lines.japanese: 「もー無理もー無理！　まじでまじで、早く止めれって部外者！」
lines.english: “He can’t, he can’t! Seriously, seriously, hurry up and stop them, Outsider!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　やだよめんどくせえ。つか、すでにこんな空気で、いまさら止められるわけねーじゃん。んな、ほっとけって。だいたい当人たちがやりたくてやってんだし」
lines.english: “Huh? No way. Too much trouble. Besides, with the room like this, how the hell is anybody supposed to stop it now? Leave them alone. They’re doing it because they both want to.”

lines.japanese: 俺は馴れ馴れしい小娘の要求を突っぱねた。
lines.english: I flatly rejected the overfamiliar girl’s demand.

lines.japanese: しかし、だからと言ってツッパリ少年たちの野蛮なお遊戯にも興味はなかったので、そんじゃ膀胱タンクに溜まった元コーラでもブッ放してくるかと便所へ向かうことにした。
lines.english: That didn't mean I cared to watch the young delinquents at their savage little game, so I decided it was time to head for the john and fire off the former cola collecting in my bladder tank.
“Jeez—”

lines.japanese: 「ああん？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 小娘は俺を引きとめようとはしなかったが、俺の方を向いたまま聞こえよがしに独白を始めた。
lines.english: The girl made no move to stop me, but she turned my way and began a monologue pitched very deliberately for me to hear.

lines.japanese: 「も、なに！　なんだこれ？　ないない、マジないわ」
lines.english: “Jeez, what the hell is this? No. No way. This is seriously messed up.”

lines.japanese: やつはすっかり呆れはて、もう笑ウシカナイ状態だった。
lines.english: She was so completely appalled that she had reached the point where all she could do was laugh.

lines.japanese: 「ハハ！　何なんここ。何時代、何部族、ええッ？　なんで殴り合いのケンカがそんな、おめでたい通過儀礼みたいなことになってんだよ。おまえら全員ばかですかそうですか、じゃゴム紐付けて崖から飛んでろ！」
lines.english: “Ha! What is this place? What century? What tribe? Huh? How did a fistfight turn into some great big happy rite of passage? Oh, so every one of you is an idiot? Cool. Strap on bungee cords and jump off a cliff!”

lines.japanese: 「同感」
lines.english: “Agreed.”

lines.japanese: 「ハぁ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 舌打ち感覚で呟いたら聞こえてしまったらしく、小娘のふてくされた目がこちらを睨んできた。俺は視線を逸らせて後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: I muttered it like a click of the tongue, but apparently she heard. The girl's sulky eyes snapped around to glare at me. I looked away and scratched hard at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「いや、だって、それがまっとうな反応だと思うし」
lines.english: “I mean, that’s the sane reaction.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ぁ……だしょ？　そだしょ！？　思うだしょフツー！　ねね、じゃあ早く──」
lines.english: “Ah... right? It is, right!? That's what any normal person would think! Hey, hey, so hurry up and—”

lines.japanese: 「いや、思うけどさ。でも子供のケンカ大人が止めたって、ロクなことンなんねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Yeah, sure. But when adults step in to break up a kids' fight, it never ends well.”

lines.japanese: 「むしろあとでこっそり再開されるよか、ここで気ィ済むまでやらせといた方が何かと安全なんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Safer all around to let them get it out of their systems here than have them sneak off and start again later, isn’t it?”
“Nnngh... ghhh...”

lines.japanese: やつは口をつぐんで俺を睨んだ。そんなもん怖くもないので鬼スルー。
lines.english: She clamped her mouth shut and glared at me. As if that could scare me. I ignored her completely.

lines.japanese: 「あぁ！　ああ～ハイそおですねーっ！」
lines.english: “Oh! Okaaay, fine!”

lines.japanese: そして小娘逆ギレ。
lines.english: And now the girl turned her anger on me.

lines.japanese: 「ハーッ！　そおですね・もお知らね。はーバカらし、やってられんしー」
lines.english: “Hah! Fine, then! See if I care. God, this is so stupid. I’m done with it.”

lines.japanese: 「あーウン、そーじゃんそーじゃん。よく考えたらカズ君どうなったって、べつに私が困ることひとつもないじゃん。あっ、なんだなんだ良かってぃ～♪　心配とか全然ゼロ意味、ノープレだはッハ～ン♪」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah, right, exactly. Now that I think about it, there isn’t one single way Kazu getting wrecked causes me any trouble. Oh! Well, isn’t that ni-i-ice! ♪ Worrying was total zero-meaning. No play, ha-haaan! ♪”

lines.japanese: 今度は優雅に舞いながら笑ってる。忙しいやつだ。俺は輪の中の試合状況を覗きながら言った。
lines.english: Now she was laughing and dancing with theatrical grace. Busy girl. I peered into the ring to see how things were going and said:

lines.japanese: 「おー、でも、意外に粘ってんぞおまえの彼氏」
lines.english: “Hey, your boyfriend’s hanging in there better than I expected.”

lines.japanese: 「ぜんぜん・彼氏じゃ・ないから！」
lines.english: “He is! Not! My boyfriend!”

lines.japanese: 「今だって、終電乗りすごしてなかったら私、こんなとこいないし。翔さんのゲストってことでタダにしてもらったけど、そうじゃなかったらひとりで漫喫かファミレス行ってるよ」
lines.english: “If I hadn't missed the last train, I wouldn't even be here right now. Kakeru got me in free as his guest, but otherwise I'd be spending the night by myself at an all-night comic café or a family restaurant.”

lines.japanese: 「あーでも、かなり足にキてんなあ、おまえの彼氏」
lines.english: “Yeah, but your boyfriend’s legs are looking pretty shaky now.”

lines.japanese: 「聞けよ！」
lines.english: “Listen to me!”

lines.japanese: 「ぼおっ！」
lines.english: “Bwoof!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ボディ入った」
lines.english: “Oh. Body shot.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”
“Haaah!”

lines.japanese: ギャル男はおそらく有段者だ。二本の腕を交差させてから気合を発する、その一連の流れがサマになっていた。一方、すでに茶ロンゲはまともに歩けてすらいない。もはや勝敗は誰の目にも明らかだった。
lines.english: The party boy probably held a black belt. The whole sequence—crossing his arms, then loosing his battle cry—looked practiced and sharp. The brown-haired kid, on the other hand, could no longer even walk properly. By now the outcome was plain to everyone.

lines.japanese: しかし喰らっても喰らっても立ちむかう、倒されても倒されても起きあがる挑戦者の往生際の悪さは、ダサくてクサくて痛々しいものながら、ギャラリーからはブーイングひとつ飛んじゃいなかった。
lines.english: But the challenger kept coming no matter how many blows he took, kept rising no matter how many times he fell. It was lame, corny, painful to watch—and yet not one boo came from the gallery.

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと。どんな感じなん」
lines.english: “H-hey. What’s it looking like?”

lines.japanese: 口を尖らせた小娘が、爪先立って首を伸ばしながら言う。
lines.english: The girl pursed her lips and asked while craning her neck on tiptoe.

lines.japanese: 「なに。やっぱ気になんの」
lines.english: “What, you care after all?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに」
lines.english: “Not really.”

lines.japanese: きっぱり否定しながらも、やつは俺の肩に手を置き、それを支えに爪先立ち状態を維持していた。
lines.english: Her denial was emphatic, but she put a hand on my shoulder and used me for balance as she stayed on tiptoe.

lines.japanese: 勝手に触んなとも思ったけど、なんだかんだ言って彼氏が気になるんだろう。俺も鬼じゃないから、そのぐらいは見過ごしてやることにした。
lines.english: Part of me wanted to tell her to keep her hands to herself, but for all her carrying on, she was obviously worried about her boyfriend. I wasn't a monster. I let that much slide.

lines.japanese: 「まあダイジョブだろ、死にゃしねえよ。あのチャラい空手小僧、分かってるし。はん、見た目すげー派手に動いてっけど、ちゃんと素人相手に加減して……あー、あん？」
lines.english: “He’ll be fine. It’s not gonna kill him. That flashy little karate brat knows what he’s doing. Hnh. Looks like he’s throwing himself around something fierce, but he’s pulling his punches against an amateur… Ah? Wait.”

lines.japanese: ふとチャラ手小僧の挙動が気になった。わざわざ真っ向から相手の正面ばかり攻めている。素人の正面以外なんてガラ空きなのに。
lines.english: Something about the karate brat's movement caught my eye. He was going out of his way to attack strictly head-on, even though every side but the front lay wide open against an amateur.

lines.japanese: なんだ。ああ。要するにコレ……見せ稽古か？
lines.english: What? Oh. So that's what this is... a demonstration bout?

lines.japanese: 「オルァ、休んでんじゃねーぞザコがァ！」
lines.english: “Get up, scrub! No taking a breather!”

lines.japanese: 「たりめーだ……まだまだ、イケるっつうの……」
lines.english: “No shit... I’ve still got plenty... left in me...”

lines.japanese: 挑戦者の呼吸が荒く乱れ、腫れたまぶたの下で凄惨な眼光がきらめき、切れた鼻や口から血しぶきが飛びはじめると、いつしか野次馬から湧きおこる歓声のほとんどは好奇の冷やかしでなく純粋な激励に変わっていた。
lines.english: The challenger’s breath came ragged and wild. A savage light flashed beneath his swollen lids, and blood began flying from his split nose and lips. Somewhere along the way, nearly every shout from the onlookers had changed from jeering curiosity into honest encouragement.

lines.japanese: みんないつの間にか、弱くて無様でカッコ悪い、挑戦者にばかり声援を送っている。判官びいきの日本人。俺はレゲエ野郎のくだらない冗談を思いかえしていた。
lines.english: Before anyone knew it, they were all cheering for the challenger—the weak, pathetic, hopeless-looking one. The Japanese and their love of an underdog. I remembered the reggae freak's stupid joke.

lines.japanese: かつて自分の中でも震えていた、あの懐かしいヴァイブス。
lines.english: Those old vibes that once trembled inside me too.

lines.japanese: はん、優しい先輩たちだこと。あの坊っちゃん特待生に、男を上げる機会を与えてやったのか。はいはい美談美談。
lines.english: Hnh. What kindhearted older boys. They'd given their pampered scholarship boy a chance to prove himself a man. Yes, yes. Beautiful story.

lines.japanese: 「ねーちょっと、まだ終わらんのー」
lines.english: “Hey, is it still not over?”

lines.japanese: 便所へ行こうとしたら何故か俺にひっついてくる小娘。
lines.english: For some reason, the girl had latched onto me when I tried to head for the bathroom.

lines.japanese: 「っせえな……そんな気になんなら、おまえも応援してやりゃいいじゃん」
lines.english: “You’re such a pain... If you’re that worried, why don’t you cheer him on?”

lines.japanese: 「しない。むしろ罵倒したいかもだ、へん、ばーかばーか！」
lines.english: “No. If anything, I feel like insulting him. Hmph. Stupid, stupid!”

lines.japanese: 「ハーあんな、血ぃダラ～垂らしちゃって、もーマジ引くんですけど。なにあれ、どーしたいワケ？　１００パー勝てないのに、超～ムキんなっちゃって、男ってもーホント意味ワカラ～ン」
lines.english: “I mean, ugh, look at him, bleeding all over the place. It's seriously gross. What is he even trying to accomplish? There's a hundred-percent chance he loses, but he's getting *so* worked up over it. I swear, men make zero seeeense.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まあなあ」
lines.english: “Mm. Yeah, fair.”

lines.japanese: 俺のプラカップには、すでに氷すら残っていなかった。なんとなく口まわりが退屈で、舌先でなんとなく頬の裏側を撫でた。
lines.english: Not even the ice remained in my plastic cup. My mouth felt vaguely idle, so for no particular reason I ran my tongue along the inside of my cheek.

lines.japanese: 「まあなあじゃなくて、私訊いてんの。なんで勝てないの分かってて、あんな諦め悪いの」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘yeah, fair’ me. I’m asking you. If he knows he can’t win, why is he so desperate not to give up?”

lines.japanese: 「え゛ー？　あー、そーなあ、知んねーけど……」
lines.english: “Ehh? Ahh, well... I dunno, but...”

lines.japanese: 俺は想像力を働かせて言った。
lines.english: I put my imagination to work.

lines.japanese: 「んー、アレじゃん。要は、ここにいたいんじゃねーの、あいつ」
lines.english: “Mm. Maybe that’s it. Maybe he just wants to stay here—with them.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なにが？　いるじゃん。え、いるじゃん。いればいいじゃん、フツーに」
lines.english: “Huh? What do you mean? He's here. Look, he's right here. So he can just be here. Normally.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、フツーにいんのが難しンじゃん。子供だってクラスの会話に置いてかれんのヤで、べつに見たくもねー番組ムリクリ見たりすんだろ」
lines.english: “That's the point. Maybe it's hard for him to just be there like everyone else. Kids hate getting left out of conversations at school, so they'll force themselves to watch shows they don't even wanna see, right?”

lines.japanese: 俺はまず千歳鷲介のへらへら顔を念頭に置き、それを嘲るように言った。
lines.english: The grinning face of Shusuke Chitose came first to mind, and I said it almost in mockery of him.

lines.japanese: 「そういうさ、いんだよ、たまに。そこに馴染みたくて頑張っちゃう臆病なンが」
lines.english: “You get people like that sometimes. Cowards who try too hard because they want to fit in.”
“Mmmm...?”

lines.japanese: 女は下唇を噛んで首をひねった。そしてしばらく唸ってから──
lines.english: The girl bit her lower lip and tilted her head. After mulling it over with a low groan—

lines.japanese: 「ふウ～ん？」
lines.english: “Hmmm, really?”

lines.japanese: ──妙な節付きの生ぬるい相槌を打ってよこした。
lines.english: —she gave me that lukewarm acknowledgment in a peculiar little singsong.

lines.japanese: 「えー、でもワカラ～ン。べつに観てる番組なんてカブんなくたって、話ぐらいいくらでも出来なくない？　てか、テレビしか話題ないとかその前提そもそもおかしいって」
lines.english: “Ehh, I still don't get it. You don't have to watch the same shows to find a million things to talk about, do you? Besides, the whole premise that TV is your only conversation topic is already messed up.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「てゆか決め打ちの会話リアルで狙ったら、八割外すでしょ。やっぱビミョーに芝居くさくなるし、流れとか自然じゃなくなるし、そんで気付かれたら超寒いで、もイイことないって。会話なんてバメンでいんぢゃん？」
lines.english: “I mean, if you go into a real conversation aiming for one specific canned exchange, you'll miss eight times out of ten. It starts feeling kind of rehearsed, the flow stops being natural, and if they notice, it gets *so* embarrassing. There's literally no upside. Why not just talk about whatever fits the moment?”

lines.japanese: 「あそ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: たとえ話の分からないやつだ。
lines.english: This girl did not understand analogies.

lines.japanese: 「おまえは幸せだな。あんま悩みとかねーだろ」
lines.english: “You must lead a happy life. Bet you don’t have much to worry about.”

lines.japanese: 「ハあっ！？　何その上から目線、むっかつくー、部外者ちょお暴言ザウルス。もー初対面でいきなしそゆこと言ぅーなしー！」
lines.english: “Hah!? What's with the condescending crap? God, you piss me off. Outsider, you're a total Insultosaurus! You don't just say stuff like that the first time you meet somebody!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、すんませんしたねえ、そりゃ」
lines.english: “Ahh, terribly sorry about that.”

lines.japanese: 馴れ馴れしい猫パンチが飛んできそうだったから、適当に引きさがった。小娘は振りあげた手を下ろして、俺に裏返しの人差し指を向ける。
lines.english: She looked about to swat me with that overfamiliar little cat-paw again, so I halfheartedly backed off. The brat lowered her raised hand, flipped it over, and pointed a finger at me.

lines.japanese: 「えーえー？　じゃそっちは？　そっちもやっぱ、そーゆータイプなん？」
lines.english: “Oho? Then what about you? Are you that type too?”

lines.japanese: 「俺？　あァ、俺はまあ……みんながテレビ観てても、自分だけラジオ聴いてるようなやつだから」
lines.english: “Me? Ahh, well... I’m the kind of guy who listens to the radio when everybody else is watching TV.”

lines.japanese: 「ぷはっ、何それ超うけるー」
lines.english: “Pfft! What does that even mean? That’s hilarious!”

lines.japanese: 小娘は手をバッチバチ叩いて豪快に笑った。五分咲きの笑顔には小さな八重歯が浮かんでいた。
lines.english: The girl clapped her hands sharply and laughed without restraint. A tiny snaggletooth showed in her half-blooming smile.

lines.japanese: ゲロとイカと安酒の臭いがする街で育った俺は、口元に手を添えて楚々とはにかむような出来た女が苦手だから、こんな気持ちのいい笑い方をする子供がわりと好きだった。
lines.english: I grew up in a town that smelled of puke, squid, and cheap booze, so I'd never cared for polished women who covered their mouths and tittered with ladylike reserve. I rather liked kids who laughed this openly.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なに。今度はなんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What. What is it now?”

lines.japanese: 「てことは部外者、友達いない系？」
lines.english: “So, Outsider... are you the type who doesn't have any friends?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～？　友達も彼女もいない系ッ？　ひとりで水族館とか行っちゃう系ッ！？」
lines.english: “Ooh? The type with no friends *or* girlfriend? The type who goes to aquariums all by himself!?”

lines.japanese: 俺はゆっくりと、あたかも葉巻を吸って吐いて揉みけすぐらいの速度で、おもむろに視線を戻した。
lines.english: Slowly—as slowly as if I were drawing on a cigar, breathing it out, and grinding the stub dead—I brought my gaze back around.

lines.japanese: そして氷の鳴らないプラカップを唇へ押しつけ、正面の闇を睨みながら呟く。
lines.english: Then I pressed the iceless plastic cup to my lips and muttered while glaring into the dark ahead.

lines.japanese: 「よせよ。系って言葉は好きじゃない」
lines.english: “Knock it off. I don't like the word *type*.”

lines.japanese: その晩、大方の予想通り、茶髪のロンゲは銀髪のロンゲに大敗を喫した。
lines.english: That night, just as most people expected, the brown-haired longhair suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of the silver-haired one.

lines.japanese: 大した攻防もなく、終始一方的な戦いだった。最後は結局、勝者ギャル男が昭和の熱血番長よろしく「今日はこのぐらいで勘弁してやらあ」的な情けをかけた感じの幕引きだった。
lines.english: There wasn’t much give-and-take. The fight was one-sided from beginning to end. At last the victorious pretty boy brought down the curtain with the mercy of some hot-blooded Showa-era schoolyard tough: I’ll let you off with that much for today.

lines.japanese: しまいにゃ昭和ついでに、勝者が敗者へ肩を貸し、その青春ドラマ風お約束に野次馬が拍手と声援とあったかい微笑みを送るなんていう、冗談みたいな美談にまとまっていた。
lines.english: And to complete the old-school throwback, the winner lent the loser his shoulder while the spectators applauded, cheered, and smiled warmly at that stock teen-drama ending. The whole thing wrapped itself into a heartwarming tale so neat it had to be a joke.

lines.japanese: めでたくなし、めでたくなし。
lines.english: And they did not live happily ever after. Not happily ever after at all.

lines.japanese: （ついでに大方の予想通りがもうひとつ。そのヘテロなんたらいう胡散臭いクラブは、案の定それから３ヵ月後に警察の指導が入ってあっけなく営業停止を食らったそうな。その後どうなったかは知らない）
lines.english: (And one more thing turned out just as everybody expected: three months later, that shady club with the Hetero-whatever name apparently received a visit from the police and was promptly shut down. No idea what happened after that.)

lines.japanese: それ以来、俺が夜の柳木原をぶらぶら歩いていると、しばしば連中に遭遇することがあった。
lines.english: After that, whenever I wandered Yanagihara at night, I would often run into the crew.

lines.japanese: 頼んでもいないのに、やつらは勝手に声をかけてきちゃ足を止める。
lines.english: Without the slightest invitation, they would call out to me and stop me for a chat.

lines.japanese: 覚えたくもないのに、何人かについては顔や名前まで覚えてしまった。
lines.english: Without the slightest desire to learn them, I ended up remembering a few faces and names.

lines.japanese: とりわけ連中の大ボス、ホスト顔の皇帝は、例の芝居がかった声と口調で意味不明の冷やかしを残していって俺をげんなりさせる。うざい。ハイパーうざい。
lines.english: Their big boss in particular—the host-faced Emperor—would drop some incomprehensible tease in that theatrical voice of his and leave me exhausted. Annoying. Hyper-annoying.

lines.japanese: そんなうざい連中をしっしと払いのけながら、今日も俺は繁華街・柳木原のネオンの下で生きている。だってここが俺の遊び場であり職場なんだから仕方がない。
lines.english: And so, shooing those annoying bastards away, I live on beneath the neon of Yanagihara's entertainment district to this day. Can't be helped. This is my playground, and it's where I work.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうだ、職場といえば。
lines.english: Oh, right. Speaking of work.

lines.japanese: なあ、おまえ。もしなにか、自分の手が回らない、ちょっとした用事があれば言ってくれ。交通費込みで時給９００円いただければ、誠心誠意お手伝いさせていただこう。
lines.english: Hey, you. If there’s some little errand you can’t find the time to handle yourself, let me know. Nine hundred yen an hour, travel included, and I’ll give it my honest best.

lines.japanese: そんな「街の便利屋さん」が俺の副業だ。ただしエージは通さないでくれ。やつからの紹介なら、たぶん俺は断るだろう。
lines.english: That's my sideline: your friendly neighborhood handyman. Just don't come through Eiji. If he sends you, I'll probably turn you down.

lines.japanese: いいか？　ピンフ通りの中ほどに、なかなか美味いクレープを食わせてくれるピンクのミニバンが停まってるはずだ。そこの若い女店主が、成田工務店（通称）の窓口になってる。
lines.english: Got it? Halfway down Pinfu Street, there should be a pink minivan selling some pretty damn good crêpes. The young woman who owns it handles the front desk for Narita Construction—unofficial name.

lines.japanese: え……ああ、メインの収入源？　いや、それはまあ、なんだ、普通のバイトだけど。
lines.english: Huh...? Oh, my main source of income? No, that's, well... just ordinary part-time work.

lines.japanese: 工事現場の作業補助とか、建築現場のガラ出しとか、デパートの搬出搬入とか……要するにカラダを使う仕事が基本だな。
lines.english: Helping out on road crews, clearing rubble from construction sites, loading and unloading at department stores... Manual labor, basically.

lines.japanese: だけど、まあアレだ、メインの仕事はさ……ぶっちゃけ、なかなか長くは続かないんだよ。いや、まあ、色々あってな。色々。そう色々。
lines.english: But, well, here's the thing. Those main jobs... honestly, they never last very long. No, see, stuff happens. Lots of stuff. Yeah. Stuff.

lines.japanese: っせえな、いいんだよ。探偵とか便利屋の稼業はハードボイルドの基本だろ。俺は基本に忠実なんだよ。文句あんのかてめえ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。
lines.english: Shut up, it’s fine. Detectives and handymen are hard-boiled staples. I’m faithful to the fundamentals. Got a problem with that? I’ll fucking kill you, asshole.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか。そういや、そうだな。
lines.english: Oh. Right. Come to think of it, yeah.

lines.japanese: そうだ、さっきからどっかのイカレポンチの話ばっかりで、まだ俺のことをあんまり話してなかったわな。
lines.english: That's right. I've done nothing but talk about some lunatic for a while now. Haven't told you much about me yet, have I?

lines.japanese: おし、分かった。
lines.english: Okay. Got it.

lines.japanese: なあ、おまえ、どうせ暇なんだろ？
lines.english: Hey, you’ve got nothing better to do anyway, right?

lines.japanese: ちょっと遠まわしになるけど聞いてけよ。おいそれと他のやつには語れないこともあるけど、おまえになら、まあ、少しずつだけど話してやってもいい。
lines.english: This may be a roundabout way to tell it, but hear me out. There are things I can’t go telling just anybody. But you… well, maybe I could tell you, little by little.

lines.japanese: よし。じゃあアレだ、俺の──俺たちの物語を始めよう。
lines.english: All right. Then let's begin my—our story.

lines.japanese: ひとつ、まあ、よろしくっつーことで。
lines.english: So... here's hoping we get along.

lines.japanese: ……で、おまえ誰？
lines.english: ...Anyway, who are you?
